issues.legal_issue: A defendant omitted because of a good-faith mistake may be treated as joined from the original filing when the omission is promptly corrected and the suit would have been timely against that defendant.
material_facts: The plaintiff relied on a certified copy of the sale deed that named only the two defendants already sued, although the original deed also named another purchaser.

The existing defendants did not identify the omitted purchaser in their written statement or produce the original deed with it; her name became known when their counsel read from the original in court.
The plaintiff applied to add her as a defendant the next day, and the Court found that he had acted with due care and attention and had no reason or motive to omit her.
The Court found that the suit would have been within the limitation period if the omitted purchaser had been joined when it was originally filed.
issues.conclusion: The omission was a mistake made in good faith, so the suit against the added defendant was deemed instituted on the original filing date and was not barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 21(1) of the Limitation Act, 1963, its proviso permits a court satisfied that omission of a defendant resulted from a mistake made in good faith to deem the suit against that defendant instituted on an earlier date. Section 2(h) defines good faith as acting with due care and attention. The proviso softens the former rule in Section 22 of the Limitation Act, 1908, under which a suit against an added defendant was deemed instituted only when that defendant was added. Article 97 governs limitation for enforcing a right of pre-emption. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: pre_emption_suit and additional_defendant_omitted_by_mistake and plaintiff_relied_on_available_official_record and plaintiff_lacked_other_notice and plaintiff_corrected_omission_promptly and omission_made_with_due_care and original_filing_timely_against_additional_defendant

predicates.pre_emption_suit: The proceeding is a suit to enforce a right of pre-emption.
predicates.additional_defendant_omitted_by_mistake: The plaintiff left out a person who should have been named as a defendant because of a mistake.
predicates.plaintiff_relied_on_available_official_r: The plaintiff relied on an official record available to him that did not disclose the omitted defendant's interest.
predicates.plaintiff_lacked_other_notice: The plaintiff had no other notice of the omitted defendant's interest before the omission was discovered.
predicates.plaintiff_corrected_omission_promptly: The plaintiff sought to add the omitted defendant promptly after learning of the omission.
predicates.omission_made_with_due_care: The plaintiff acted with due care and attention in omitting the defendant.
predicates.original_filing_timely_against_additiona: The suit would have been within the applicable limitation period against the additional defendant if she had been joined at the outset.
predicates.additional_defendant_treated_as_joined_o: The suit against the additional defendant is treated as instituted on the original filing date.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff in a pre-emption suit carefully relies on an official record, lacks other notice, and promptly corrects a resulting mistaken omission, the added defendant may be treated as joined on the original filing date if the suit would then have been timely.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser who is necessary to the complete adjudication of a pre-emption suit must be joined, and adding that purchaser does not require an amendment to the pleaded cause-of-action date when relation back resolves the limitation issue.
material_facts: The omitted person was also a purchaser of the land that was the subject of the pre-emption suit.
The Court found that she was a necessary party for the court to effectually and completely adjudicate and settle the questions in the suit.
The application sought to add her as a defendant and also to amend the pleaded cause-of-action date; the Court held that the latter amendment had become unnecessary.
issues.conclusion: The application to add the necessary defendant was allowed; amendment of the cause-of-action date was unnecessary, and the case was remanded for determination of the remaining issues.
issues.legal_principle: Order I Rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure permits the addition of a necessary party to enable the court effectually and completely to adjudicate upon and settle all questions involved in the suit. In this case, the date amendment under Order VI Rule 17 was unnecessary because the added defendant was treated as joined on the original filing date. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.pre_emption_suit: The proceeding is a suit to enforce a right of pre-emption.
predicates.omitted_person_was_co_purchaser: The omitted person was one of the purchasers of the property involved in the suit.
predicates.omitted_person_required_for_complete_adj: The omitted person must be joined for the court to effectually and completely resolve the questions in the suit.
predicates.original_filing_date_preserved_for_added: The suit against the added person is treated as instituted on the original filing date.
predicates.necessary_co_purchaser_must_be_added_wit: The necessary co-purchaser is added, and amendment of the cause-of-action date is unnecessary.

issues.definition: When a co-purchaser is necessary to complete adjudication and the original filing date is preserved for that person, the person must be added without amending the cause-of-action date.
